definitions.explanation: A hot pepper of the genus Capsicum, used widely in Japanese cooking as a spice. Includes both fresh and dried forms.

examples.japanese: {唐辛子|とうがらし}を{入|い}れすぎた。
examples.english: I put in too much chili pepper.

examples.japanese: うどんに{七味唐辛子|しちみとうがらし}をかけて{食|た}べる。
examples.english: I eat udon topped with seven-spice chili powder.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}で{唐辛子|とうがらし}を{栽培|さいばい}して、{乾燥|かんそう}させて{保存|ほぞん}している。
examples.english: I grow chili peppers in my garden, dry them, and store them.

notes:
The name literally means 'Tang (Chinese) mustard child,' reflecting its historical import route. In everyday usage, {唐辛子|とうがらし} can refer to both fresh chili peppers and dried/powdered chili. {七味唐辛子|しちみとうがらし} (seven-spice chili powder) and {一味唐辛子|いちみとうがらし} (pure chili powder) are common condiments on Japanese dining tables.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{七味|しちみ}{唐辛子|とうがらし} — seven-spice chili powder
・{一味|いちみ}{唐辛子|とうがらし} — pure chili powder
・{鷹|たか}の{爪|つめ} — dried whole red chili (lit. hawk's claw)
・{唐辛子|とうがらし}を{効|き}かせる — to add chili spiciness
